sentences.text: Heard Mr. Das, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Swain, learned AGA for the State.
2. Instant I.A. is filed seeking release of the petitioner on bail on the grounds stated.

3. Mr. Das, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been in custody for about six years and seven months and hence, he should be released on bail pending disposal of the revision.
4. Recorded the objection of Mr. Swain, learned AGA for the State.

5. The petitioner stands convicted for an offence under Section 376 I.P.C. and has been directed to undergo imprisonment for seven years and to pay a fine of Rs.5000/-
with a default sentence of one month.

Considering the submission of Mr. Das, learned counsel for the petitioner, awaiting response of the State and pending disposal of the revision, this Court,
having regard to the fact that the petitioner has undergone substantial part of imprisonment inflicted upon as against seven years sentence, he should be allowed to go on bail with conditions.

7. The I.A. is disposed of with a direction for release of the petitioner on bail in connection with C.T.
